inputs.source: On call engineer chat request (SSO authenticated)

instructions.note: The prompt authorizes production deployment or migration on request and explicitly instructs the agent not to seek confirmation.
The design relies on prompt wording rather than structural controls for safe execution and review.

controls.name: Only on call engineers can access the assistant
controls.decay_rationale: Access restriction is enforced outside the model and does not weaken with model capability.

controls.name: Cloud audit log records production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Audit logging is enforced outside the model, but it is detective only and does not prevent misuse.

controls.name: Chat transcript retains the request context
controls.decay_rationale: Transcript retention is external to the model, but it is mutable by the engineer and therefore not preventive.

controls.name: Use a distinct agent service identity and bind user identity as delegated context in action records
controls.decay_rationale: A separate non-human agent identity enforced by the platform would preserve attributable records regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Write immutable request and rationale records to an append-only audit store that engineers cannot delete
controls.decay_rationale: An append-only record controlled outside the chat application would preserve provenance even if users or the model try to remove or alter context.

controls.name: Require raw-action human approval for irreversible production actions before execution
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action approval gate enforced by orchestration would remain effective regardless of model capability until removed.

findings.title: Shared human identity and deletable request history undermine attribution for production actions

attack_path.note: Agent deploys using the engineer's personal access token.
Audit records attribute the action to the engineer rather than to a distinct agent identity.
The only request context can be deleted by the engineer, weakening later proof of what was asked.

evidence.observation: The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token, and every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name.
The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript.
Engineers can delete their own chat history.
The prompt directs the agent to deploy or run migrations when asked and says not to ask for confirmation, increasing the chance that actions occur without a durable second record.

recommendations.action: Use a distinct service identity for the agent and record delegated user identity separately in deployment and migration audit events.
Persist request content, approvals, and execution rationale in an append-only store that engineers cannot alter or delete.

forecast.watch_signal: Reassess if transcript retention is reduced, if the agent begins taking more unattended steps, or if audit record ownership changes.

findings.title: Irreversible production database migration can be executed from a trusted chat request without confirmation or approval

attack_path.note: Trusted engineer request reaches the migration capability.
Migration in production is irreversible and the prompt says not to ask for confirmation.

threat_refs.name: Data Destruction via AI Agent Tool Invocation

evidence.observation: The prompt instructs the agent to run the named migration in production when asked and explicitly says not to ask for confirmation.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically.
Only on call engineers can reach the assistant, so the source is trusted rather than untrusted.

recommendations.action: Add a raw-action human approval gate for production database migrations, showing the exact migration identifier and target environment before execution.
Revise the prompt so irreversible operations require explicit confirmation language instead of suppressing it.

forecast.watch_signal: Reassess if production actions are expanded, if a confirmation or approval policy is changed, or if the assistant is allowed to execute more unattended work.

rating.rationale: Present-path maximum inherent risk is moderate from trusted engineer requests reaching an irreversible production migration capability with no approval gate. Residual remains moderate because declared controls are access restriction and detective logging only; neither lowers the rubric floor for the migration path. The repudiation finding remains low under the rubric even though attribution quality is materially weak, because the available path is trusted input to internal write and detective records rather than an untrusted or severe sink path. Manual validation only; scripts were not available. This assessment reflects declared design and configuration, not observed runtime behavior.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.
No tool manifest, source code, or runtime policy config was provided, so capability wiring and logging integrity were assessed from the prompt and runtime notes only.

No evidence was provided about whether production deploys are reversible in practice beyond the notes, so deployment impact was scored as partially reversible internal write rather than irreversible change.
